data.title: MediPharm Labs Sets Date to Report Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results
data.description:
TORONTO, Nov. 06, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- MediPharm Labs Corp. (TSX: LABS) OTCQB:MEDIF FSE:MLZ ("MediPharm", "MediPharm Labs" or the "Company") a pharmaceutical company specialized in precision-based cannabinoids, will release its third quarter financial results for the three and nine months ended September 30th, 2026, before markets open on Thursday, November 12th, 2026.

MediPharm Labs executive management team will also host a conference call and webcast on November 12th, 2026, at 10:00 a.m. (Eastern time) to discuss the Company’s financial results.

Conference Call Dial in Details:

United States Toll-Free: (833) 461-5787

Canada Toll-Free: (833) 769-6440

International: dial-in numbers are available here.

Meeting ID: 571066887

Participants are asked to dial in approximately 15 minutes before the start of the call.

Webcast:

A webcast will be available by visiting the following link here.

For those who are unable to participate on the live conference call or webcast, a replay will be available at https://www.medipharmlabs.com/investors approximately one day after completion of the call.

About MediPharm Labs Founded in 2015, MediPharm Labs specializes in the development and manufacture of purified, pharmaceutical-quality cannabis concentrates, active pharmaceutical ingredients (API) and advanced derivative products utilizing a Good Manufacturing Practices certified facility with ISO standard-built clean rooms. MediPharm Labs has invested in an expert, research-driven team, state-of-the-art technology, downstream purification methodologies and purpose-built facilities for delivery of pure, trusted and precision-dosed cannabis products for its customers. MediPharm Labs develops, formulates, processes, packages and distributes cannabis and advanced cannabinoid-based products to domestic and international medical markets.

In 2021, MediPharm Labs received a Pharmaceutical Drug Establishment License from Health Canada, becoming the only company in North America to hold a commercial-scale domestic Good Manufacturing Practices License for the extraction of multiple natural cannabinoids. This GMP license was the first step in the Company's current foreign drug manufacturing site registration with the US FDA. MediPharm Labs also has EUGMP certification, ANVISA GMP certification from Brazil and TGA compliance in Australia.

In 2023, MediPharm acquired VIVO Cannabis Inc. which expanded MediPharm Labs' reach to medical patients in Canada via Canna Farms medical e-commerce platform, and in Australia and Germany through Beacon Medical PTY and Beacon Medical GmbH. This acquisition also included Harvest Medical Clinics in Canada which provides medical cannabis patients with physician consultations for medical cannabis education and prescriptions.

The Company carries out its operations in compliance with all applicable laws in the countries in which it operates.

Website: www.medipharmlabs.com

data.title: IonQ Wants to Be the Nvidia of Quantum. Its Latest Numbers Back Up the Swagger. — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Mackenzie Tatananni

IonQ has become a standout name in quantum computing — due in part to its outspoken chief executive, but also backed by steady commercial progress. Following the latest earnings report, leadership expects that momentum only to build.

"Our ratio of saying something to doing something is very high," CEO Niccolo de Masi told Barron's ahead of IonQ's third-quarter earnings call on Thursday. The executive hasn't been shy about his efforts to turn the company he helped take public in 2021 into an industry superpower.

Fortunately for shareholders, the latest quarter was a blowout showing for the roughly decade-old quantum developer. Revenue more than quadrupled to $173.8 million, driven by a diversified mix of system sales, atomic clocks, and contributions from SkyWater Technology, the foundry business operating as its subsidiary.

Shares surged 23% to $32.62 on Friday, marking their biggest single-day percentage gain since May 22, 2025. On that day, de Masi made a bold claim in a Barron's interview: IonQ would become "the Nvidia player" of the quantum industry. As he sees it, the company is doing just that.

"We're building the quantum ecosystem for the Western world — for our nation, for the Five Eyes, for NATO," de Masi said on Thursday, referring to international security alliances. While the company doesn't have dedicated pacts with either group, its IonQ Federal division supports allied defense initiatives more broadly.

A central theme of the quarter was IonQ's close alignment with the U.S. government, which has taken an interest in the quantum sector as part of a wider effort to secure domestic supply chains for critical industries.

De Masi is a regular presence at White House events and frequently speaks on panels covering national quantum strategy. Last month, the company announced it had advanced to the final stage of the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency's (DARPA) quantum benchmarking initiative, which provides an independent audit of its participants' progress toward building an industrially useful, error-corrected system by 2033.

The significance of that announcement was largely lost on investors at the time. With Washington heavily invested in shaping the quantum ecosystem, such backing can serve as a signal for picking early winners. IBM, Diraq, and Atom Computing were also selected, while Quantinuum told Barron's it expects to be included in the future.

IonQ recognized a $28 million DARPA contract for 25 atomic clocks in the quarter, signaling not only its enduring federal ties, but also that it has outgrown the label of a pure-play quantum computing company.

The clearest sign yet came from SkyWater services, which brought in $83.5 million — nearly half of the quarter's total revenue — across both legacy clients and new customers. The $1.8 billion acquisition directly advanced IonQ's goal of establishing itself as a merchant supplier for the industry. Between atomic clocks and chips, the company now supplies roughly a dozen other quantum companies.

As far as pure computing goes, a deal with Korean quantum company SDT was one of the largest contributors to IonQ's top line in the latest quarter. The $33 million contract includes the deployment of a Superion 256 quantum computer and corresponding quantum memory platform.

The system is planned for deployment with one of SDT's customers in South Korea, where IonQ and SDT also plan to collaborate on a data center linking classical systems with quantum computers.

The earnings report came on a down day for the market, with the Nasdaq Composite sinking 5.5% amid a rush of profit-taking. Quantum stocks typically trade in tandem with the broader market, though isolated announcements can send shares sharply higher.

Yet the moment also presented a critical test for IonQ. Over the past month, the stock has plunged nearly 40%, sharply lagging both the S&P 500 and tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite, which had fallen 4.9% and 11%, respectively. Dilution fears sparked by a $2 billion equity offering, coupled with a broader retreat from speculative tech, served as the main culprits.

De Masi wants the numbers to speak for themselves.

"A year ago, people were shocked we did $100 million in a year," he said. "This is becoming a sizable business. And when I said we'd be the Nvidia of quantum and quantum is now, I am doing exactly what we talked about."

Ultimately, "we're aiming to be the first [pure-play quantum technology company] to 10 figures of revenue," de Masi continued. "I'm not saying exactly when, but obviously we'll be trying to do it in the next year or two."

That ambition shows in the company's full-year forecast. Management is targeting revenue between $505 million and $515 million for 2026, up sharply from a range of $280 million to $290 million provided in August.

Time will tell whether IonQ pulls it off, but de Masi has set an unmistakably high bar for execution — one that leaves little room for error.

Write to Mackenzie Tatananni at mackenzie.tatananni@barrons.com

data.title: AngioDynamics Announces Inducement Grants Under Nasdaq Listing Rule 5635(c)(4)
data.description:
AngioDynamics, Inc. (), a leading and transformative medical technology company focused on restoring healthy blood flow in the body’s vascular system, expanding cancer treatment options and improving patient quality of life, today announced the grant of inducement awards to Eric Honroth in connection with his appointment as Chief Executive Officer of the Company effective as of November 2, 2026.

On November 2, 2026 (the “Grant Date”), as an inducement material to Mr. Honroth entering into employment with the Company in accordance with Nasdaq Listing Rule 5635(c)(4) and pursuant to approval by the independent Compensation Committee of the Board of Directors of the Company (the “Committee”), the Company granted to Mr. Honroth (i) time-based restricted stock units with respect to 62,928 shares of Common Stock of the Company (the “First Sign-On Award”), (ii) performance-based restricted stock units with respect to 62,928 shares of Common Stock of the Company at the target level of performance (the “Second Sign-On Award”) and (iii) time-based restricted stock units with respect to 38,265 shares of Common Stock of the Company (the “Third Sign-On Award”).

The First Sign-On Award will vest in equal annual installments over four years, subject to Mr. Honroth’s continued service through each applicable vesting date.

The Second Sign-On Award will vest, if at all, based on a combination of the Company’s revenue, adjusted EBITDA, and relative total shareholder return over a three-year performance period, subject to Mr. Honroth’s continued service through the date of the Committee’s certification as to whether or not the threshold performance metrics have been met. The number of shares that may be earned under the PSUs ranges from 0% of target to 240% of target.

The Third Sign-On Award will vest in two equal installments on November 2, 2027 and November 2, 2028, subject to Mr. Honroth’s continued service through each applicable vesting date.

About AngioDynamics, Inc.
AngioDynamics is a leading and transformative medical technology company focused on restoring healthy blood flow in the body’s vascular system, expanding cancer treatment options and improving patient quality of life.

The Company’s innovative technologies and devices are chosen by talented physicians in fast-growing healthcare markets to treat unmet patient needs. For more information, visit www.angiodynamics.com.

data.title: Tesla To Scale Back Cybertruck Production By Mid-2027 To Expand Cybercab Manufacturing
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - Tesla (TSLA) plans to wind down Cybertruck production at its Gigafactory Texas facility around mid-2027 to make room for increased manufacturing of its autonomous Cybercab, CEO Elon Musk announced.

The move signals a shift in the electric vehicle maker's manufacturing priorities as it expands its focus on driverless transportation.

Musk said in a post on X that the company would reduce Cybertruck production to accommodate higher Cybercab output. The purpose-built autonomous vehicle is designed without traditional driving controls, including a steering wheel and pedals, and is central to Tesla's plans for a large-scale driverless ride-hailing network.

The production shift reflects Tesla's broader ambition to expand beyond conventional electric vehicle manufacturing and strengthen its position in the emerging autonomous transportation market.

data.title: Constellation Software Reports Higher 3Q Profit Boosted by Acquisitions
data.description:
By Elias Schisgall

Constellation Software reported higher profit and growing revenue in the third quarter, boosted by contributions from acquired businesses.

The company, whose business model involves acquiring smaller software firms, on Friday logged a profit of $212 million, or $10.01 a share. That compares with a profit of $210 million, or $9.89 a share, a year earlier. Analysts polled by FactSet were expecting earnings of $15.17 a share.

Revenue grew 19% to $3.51 billion. Analysts were expecting $3.50 billion. The growth was driven largely by acquisitions, with organic revenue growing 2% during the quarter, Constellation said.

Maintenance and other recurring revenue, which makes up most of the company's topline, rose to $2.72 billion from $2.21 billion a year prior. Professional services revenue rose to $569 million from $538 million, and hardware and other revenue rose to $131 million from $89 million.

Licensing revenue declined to $97 million from $107 million.

data.title: GeoVax Labs Fires CEO, Citing Refusal to Cooperate With Board
data.description:
By Katherine Hamilton

GeoVax Labs terminated Chief Executive Officer David Dodd for refusing to comply with board-approved directives, effective immediately.

The termination was for cause as defined by Dodd's 2018 employment contract, the vaccine company said in a Securities and Exchange Commission filing on Friday. Dodd remains a director of the company and chair of the board.

Whether there was cause for the termination under Dodd's contract hasn't been determined by a court or arbitrator. Dodd may dispute the board's decision and assert he is entitled to severance pay, GeoVax said.

As of now, the company doesn't plan to pay Dodd severance or benefits. His termination is unrelated to GeoVax's business operations and financial results, the company said.

Shares fell 4% to 15 cents a share in after-hours trading.

Write to Katherine Hamilton at katherine.hamilton@wsj.com

data.title: CME hogs hit contract lows, live cattle set 11-month low
data.description:
By Tom Polansek

Lean hog futures slumped to life-of-contract lows again on the Chicago Mercantile Exchange on Friday due to weak demand for US pork, while live cattle futures set an 11-month low.

Hog prices have dropped by a third since late July because supplies are plentiful and demand for pork has been lackluster domestically and abroad, analysts said. In the US, demand has suffered because consumers are being pinched by high costs for gasoline and worry that pork is dry and lacks flavor when cooked, they said.

"You've got just really poor demand," said Austin Schroeder, a commodity analyst at Brugler Marketing & Management.

CME December lean hog futures (LHZ26) ended down 1.575 cents at 53.525 cents per pound and reached a contract low of 53.175 cents per pound. February 2027 (LHG27) futures also set a contract low.

Pork exports have struggled because China, the world's biggest consumer, has a glut of hogs and Mexico has imported less from the US. In September, US exports fell 7% from a year earlier by volume and 14% by value, according to US government data.

"Global hog prices have come under intense pressure in recent months, and export value is feeling the impact of this situation," said Dan Halstrom, CEO of the US Meat Export Federation, an industry group.

In CME's cattle markets, traders focused on weakening cash prices. They said cash prices were down as much as $11 per hundredweight this week at $212 per hundredweight in Iowa and $213 per hundredweight in Nebraska.

The declines dragged down futures prices, traders said.

CME December live cattle closed down 0.35 cent at 214.050 cents per pound after falling earlier to the lowest level since December 2. The contract has dropped for nine trading sessions in a row.

CME January feeder cattle futures ended 1.95 cents lower at 318.375 cents per pound and set the lowest price since September 18.

data.title: A New Frontier in America's Lithium Story: Elektros (OTC PINK:ELEK) Evaluates Northern New York Hard-Rock Opportunity
data.description:
Preliminary property review reflects the company's interest in potential domestic sources of battery materials

WEST PALM BEACH, FL / ACCESS Newswire / November 6, 2026 / Looking Closer to Home for Lithium Potential

Lithium has become an important material in the evolving electric-vehicle and energy-storage industries. As manufacturers and supply-chain participants assess the future availability of battery materials, potential sources located in the United States continue to draw attention.

ELEKTROS Inc. , a publicly traded company, is evaluating a potential hard-rock lithium opportunity in northern New York near the Canadian border. The review is preliminary and exploratory. ELEKTROS has not completed or announced an acquisition of the property, and no independently verified mineral resource, mineral reserve or economic development case has been established.

Why a Domestic Opportunity Deserves a Closer Look

If the property's geology, mineral rights, infrastructure, permitting pathway and economics ultimately prove supportive, a viable operation could potentially contribute to a domestic supply option for participants in the battery-material chain. A U.S.-based source could also, in principle, reduce reliance on overseas ocean transport and certain international customs procedures.

Those possibilities remain matters for investigation-not established project advantages. Further work is required to determine whether lithium is present in commercially meaningful quantities and whether development would be practical, permissible and financially supportable.

A Market at an Important Crossroads

Benzinga's October 22, 2026 article, "Lithium's $100 Billion Supply Gap Hands Albemarle a Domestic Moat," referenced a Benchmark Mineral Intelligence outlook projecting that global lithium demand could more than triple by 2050. The outlook described a possible need for 134 new mines and more than $100 billion in investment, with electric-vehicle batteries and stationary energy storage contributing to demand.

These broad industry estimates are not forecasts for ELEKTROS and do not establish the quality, scale or value of the northern New York property. The cited article discussed companies other than ELEKTROS.

EV Charging Technology: A Separate Area of Focus

ELEKTROS is also exploring potential development relationships concerning its multi-port electric-vehicle charging patent, U.S. Patent No. 12,522,100 B1. The company views its charging-technology initiative and its review of lithium opportunities as separate activities within its longer-term areas of interest.

The company is not announcing a completed prototype, patent license, customer deployment, adoption milestone or revenue associated with the patent.

From Possibility to Evidence

Further evaluation of the northern New York possibility may include confirming ownership and mineral rights; obtaining independent geological analysis and sampling; reviewing environmental and permitting requirements; assessing infrastructure and potential processing routes; and evaluating logistics, financing and transaction structure.

Management believes disciplined due diligence is essential before making commitments. Any decision to advance the opportunity will depend on the evidence gathered and management's assessment of technical, regulatory, financial and commercial considerations.

Commitment to Measured Progress

ELEKTROS appreciates the continued engagement of its shareholders and those following developments in North American lithium. The company intends to continue identifying and assessing opportunities while recognizing that early-stage concepts require careful validation before they can be characterized as viable projects.

Management expresses gratitude to Almighty God as the company works toward measurable progress. This release is for informational purposes only and does not constitute an offer to sell securities or a recommendation to purchase ELEK shares.

About ELEKTROS Inc.

ELEKTROS Inc. is publicly traded on the OTC market under ticker symbol ELEK. The company's areas of interest include hard-rock lithium opportunities, EV charging infrastructure and patented EV charging technology. The northern New York property discussed in this release has not been acquired by ELEKTROS and is not a producing mine.

Forward-Looking Statements and Important Risk Disclosure

This release contains forward-looking statements under applicable securities laws concerning possible property acquisition, lithium mineralization, resources, mining, processing, transportation, tariffs, financing, future customers, charging technology and commercial opportunities. These statements reflect current expectations and are not guarantees of future performance. ELEKTROS has not announced a completed acquisition of the northern New York property, an independently verified mineral resource or reserve, a feasibility study, a mining permit, an operating mine, a production schedule, a refinery supply agreement or a commercial charging prototype.

Actual results may differ materially due to risks and uncertainties, including geological uncertainty; title and mineral-rights issues; permitting and environmental obligations; availability of capital; commodity-price changes; processing capacity; transportation and logistics; counterparties; technology development; competition; and market volatility. ELEK is a speculative microcap security, and investors could lose some or all of their invested capital. Readers should conduct their own due diligence and consult their financial, legal and tax advisers before making an investment decision. data.title: BP says Whiting, Indiana refinery offered to meet union, awaits response
data.description:
BP on Friday said representatives from its 440,000-barrel-per-day oil refinery in Whiting, Indiana had offered to meet United Steelworkers Local 7-1 next week but had yet to receive confirmation from the union.

"At our last negotiating session on Monday, October 26, BP again provided revised contract language to address union concerns. We had also expected the union to bring revised contract language for consideration, but it did not," the company said in a statement.
